HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 69 Case :- APPLICATION U/S 482 No. - 952 of 2023 Applicant :- Chandra Prakash Mishra And 2 Others Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Another Counsel for Applicant :- Manoj Kumar Chaudhary Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
List revised.

Heard Sri Manoj Kumar Chaudhary, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Ajai Kumar singh,
learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 who has filed counter affidavit along with vakalatnama today in Court which is taken on record, Ms. Arti Agarwal, learned counsel for the State and perused the records.

The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants Chandra Prakash Mishra, Mamta Mishra and Ganpat Mishra, with the prayer to quash the entire proceedings arising out of Case Crime No. 501 of 2019, under Sections 323, 504, 498A I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Sarnath, District Varanasi, pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate VII,
Varanasi and with further prayer to stay the further proceedings of the aforesaid case.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant argued that it is common ground between the parties that the parties have settled the dispute amicably out of court.

Learned counsel has placed para nos. 9 and 10 of the affidavit and has argued that the dispute between the applicant no. 1 and the opposite party no. 2 has been resolved and they are living together as husband and wife with their children and she does not want to pursue the matter.

It is argued that vide order dated 07.10.2021 the Family Court,
Varanasi has decided the petition for restitution of conjugal rights on the basis of compromise, copy of the said order is annexure no. 4 to the affidavit.
It is argued that therefore the impugned proceedings be quashed on the ground of compromise between the parties.
Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 could not dispute the arguments as aforesaid.

He has placed para nos. 5, 6 and 8 of the counter affidavit before the Court and states that dispute between the applicant no. 1 and the opposite party no. 2 has been resolved and they are living together as husband and wife with their children.
He further states that he has no objection if the impugned proceeding pending against the applicants is quashed.
The law with regards to quashing of a case on the basis of settlement arrived between the parties, is well settled.

The Apex Court in the cases of (1) B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another: (2003)4 SCC 675; (2) Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation : (2008) 9 SCC 677; (3) Manoj Sharma Vs. State and others: ( 2008) 16 SCC 1; (4) Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab:
(2012) 10 SCC 303; (5) Shaifullah and others Vs. State of U.P. And another: 2013 (83) ACC 278 and (6) Parbatbhai Ahir@Parbatbhai @ Bhimsinbhai Karmur and others Vs. State of Gujarat and another: (2017) 9 SCC 641 has held that the cases in which the parties have settled their grievances can be quashed.

The present application is allowed.
The proceeding of the case is hereby quashed.
